text: Jun Takahashi (高橋 盾, Takahashi Jun; IPA: [takahaɕi dʑɯɴ]; born 21 September 1969) is a Japanese fashion designer who founded the brand "UnderCover" (also rendered as "Under Cover" or "Undercover"). He was born in Kiryū, Gunma, and attended Gunma Kiryu Nishi High School. In 1988, he enrolled in Fashion Education at Bunka Fashion College. During his free time, he served as the vocal lead for the cover band "Tokyo Sex Pistols," with Vivienne Westwood as his role model. In 1993, he launched UnderCover, a high-end streetwear label for men, women, and children, and also launched Nowhere, a retail venture in Ura-Harajuku with his friend Nigo, the founder of BAPE. From 1994 to 1995, he participated in Tokyo Fashion Week, and in 1995, the Nowhere Ltd. company store opened in Harajuku. Japanese designer Rei Kawakubo, creator of Comme des Garçons, became Jun's mentor and encouraged him to move to Paris. The Paris store Colette admired his designs and invited him to present his 1998 collection "Exchange" in their store. UnderCover made its debut at Paris Fashion Week in October 2002, for the Spring/Summer 2003 season. Takahashi also develops activewear lines for men and women under the label Nike x Undercover Gyakusou in collaboration with Nike. Since 2011, he has collaborated with Uniqlo to create Uniqlo UnderCover. In 2021, he created artwork and an animated music video for "Creep (Very 2021 Rmx)," a remixed version of the 1992 Radiohead song "Creep," and Radiohead singer Thom Yorke contributed the remix to one of Takahashi's fashion shows. Takahashi is married to Morishita Riko, with whom he worked on the Uniqlo collaboration, and has a son named Rin and a daughter named Lala. In 1997, he won the New Face Prize in the Mainichi fashion grand prize sponsored by the Mainichi national daily newspaper. In 2001, he received the Grand Prize in the same award. In 2013, he won the Grand Prize in the Mainichi fashion grand prize for the second time.
